contract: An interface export is ONE quantity for every interface it monitors, named on the file's title line: "Interface Hourly 'Power Flow (MW)' Data for Year 2034". So the aggregation rule is a property of the FILE, not of the column, and it is resolved from the unit in that title. Two rules are resolved from that unit. `temporal` says how HOURS combine. `class` says how INTERFACES combine, via `spatialOf` in src/tables/interface/rules.ts -- EXTENSIVE and RATE may sum, INTENSIVE may not. That is a rule about the QUANTITY and never a licence to add any two paths: only a hand-authored group, each member carrying the direction it counts in, is a boundary worth summing (src/tables/interface/groups.ts). There is still no `series` key and no `weight` key. SUM means a period total over the filtered hours is meaningful; MEAN means it is not, and the stats table shows no total at all rather than a plausible wrong one. Resolution: exact match on `unit` (case-sensitive), else no rule -- an unrecognised unit gets MEAN and no total, never a guess. `quantities` is a RECORD of the columns this exporter has been seen to emit, and nothing in src/ reads it. Its job is to fail a test: tests/test_kernels_interface.mjs asserts every entry resolves to a unit this file carries a rule for, so a newly-observed column whose unit is unknown is caught when it is written down rather than discovered as a quantity missing from a groups dropdown. Add a column here when you meet one; if the test then fails, add its unit above rather than deleting the entry.

units.note: MW is a rate. Summing it over hours produces neither MW nor MWh once a filter has removed hours from the interval, so no total is offered.
A price is intensive: the sum of hourly prices is not a price. The mean over the kept hours is the unweighted mean of the hours themselves.
